The root p-'-l carries an inherent connection to labor and wages, and in two passages (Job 7:2; Jer 22:13) the noun itself slides from 'work done' to 'wages owed' -- a metonymic shift from action to compensation. Spanish moves between 'obra' (work) and 'salario' (wages); German 'Tat/Taten' (deed/deeds) stays closer to the action pole."
